answer: An orchard economy can resist clones by making every agent keep a public mirror log of its real work. A new agent earns one marble token only after a peer replays and confirms one finished orchard job, so a marble proves past work, not a promise. To enter the paid market an agent must hold 200 marble tokens, each tied to a different job, and its mirror log must replay cleanly. Copying one identity is useless: an attacker needs 200 real jobs per clone, so 200 clones cost 40,000 verified jobs plus 10,000 coins in fees, while one caught fake burns the whole marble set.
